author: Jerome

passages.original: Legat et ipsius Hilarii libellos, quos adversus nos de haereticis rebaptizandis edi- dit, et ibi reperiet ipsum Hilarium confiteri, a Julio, Marco, Sylvestro, et caeteris veteribus epi- scopis similiter in poenitentiam omnes haereticos susceptos : nec tamen sibimet veritatis consueta- dinem praejudicare debere, Synodus quoque Ni- caena, cujus paulo ante fecimus mentionem, om- nes haereticos suscepit, exceptis Pauli. Samosateni discipulis. Et quod his majus est, episcopo Nova- tianorum, si conversus fuerit, presbyterii gradum servat. Quae sententia et Luciferum impugnat, et Hilarium : dum idem et clericus est, et baptizatus.
passages.english: Let him also read the booklets of Hilary himself, which he published against us on the rebaptizing of heretics, and there he will find Hilary himself admitting that all heretics were likewise received by way of penance by Julius, Mark, Sylvester and the other early bishops, but [arguing] that custom ought not, for all that, to prejudge the truth. The Council of Nicaea too, which we mentioned a little earlier, received all heretics, except the disciples of Paul of Samosata. And what is more than this, it preserves the rank of the presbyterate for a bishop of the Novatianists, if he has been converted. This decision refutes both Lucifer and Hilary, since the same man is both a cleric and [already] baptized.
passages.notes: "nec tamen sibimet veritatis consuetudinem praejudicare debere" is awkward as printed; translated as if "veritati" (custom should not prejudge the truth), which seems the intended sense. The Hilary here is Hilary the deacon, a Luciferian, not Hilary of Poitiers. Scanning splits (edi- dit, Ni- caena, etc.) and "consueta- dinem" for "consuetudinem" are read as the evident words.
